questions.question: What must score_decision verify before a model output can clear the decision gateway?
options: Only the point estimate, because a confident model is already calibrated
A named approver and a passing aggregate score, with no per-metric limits
Calibration, uncertainty, subgroup parity, and accountability gates that all pass
A human approval only for irreversible decisions
questions.explanation: The gateway is a conjunction of four gates. A good point estimate or a named approver cannot compensate for a failed ECE, prediction-set, or subgroup-parity check.

questions.question: Which gates fail for decision D-004, the high-risk loan application?
options: Only accountability, because the approver is present
Only uncertainty, because the prediction set is too wide
None, because the point estimate 0.68 is decisive
Calibration and subgroup parity, because ECE=0.05 and gap=0.05 exceed their 0.03 limits
questions.explanation: For HIGH_RISK, both ECE and parity tolerance are 0.03. D-004 exceeds both; its width passes and its named approver does not repair those failures.

questions.question: Why does D-005 fail its accountability gate?
options: It is IRREVERSIBLE and has no named approver
Its point estimate is below 0.95
Its prediction-set width is above 0.10
Its subgroup parity gap is above 0.02
questions.explanation: D-005 has passing calibration, uncertainty, and parity values, but approver_id is None. The irreversible branch requires a named human and rejects AUTOMATED as well.

questions.question: What does build_audit_entry record for D-003 when the approver accepts despite its failed ECE gate?
options: all_gates_passed=True and override=False
all_gates_passed=False and override=True
all_gates_passed=True and override=True
It discards the gate result once a human approver is present
questions.explanation: D-003 has ECE 0.06 above the RESOURCE_ALLOC limit 0.05, so all_gates_passed is false. A named non-AUTOMATED approver makes the gate-failure override flag true.

questions.question: When is the AuditEntry override flag set?
options: Whenever an approver_id is present, even if every gate passes
Whenever a decision is automated, because automation is an override
When at least one gate fails and a named human approver other than AUTOMATED is present
Only when the input hash cannot be computed
questions.explanation: override is defined as gate_fail and a real approver being present. It exposes a rubber stamp: a human accepted a decision that the gateway did not clear.

questions.question: Why is a high point estimate not enough to clear a high-risk decision?
options: Point estimates are ignored for every decision type
Only the model version determines whether an action can proceed
The approver may replace every metric with a personal judgement
A confident estimate can still be miscalibrated or wrong for a subgroup, so the other gates remain mandatory
questions.explanation: D-004 demonstrates the aggregate-confidence trap: the point estimate looks decisive while calibration and subgroup parity fail. The gateway keeps those safety signals independent.
